Vampiric Concerto

Summary:

Dracula, pining after the love and attention of Emma Frost, attacks Xavier's Mansion and kidnaps her girlfriend in order to make the White Queen into the Queen of the Night.

Notes:

this is a long event my friends and i did in rp

Chapter 1: 2 Minutes to Midnight

Chapter Text

In the shadowed annals of the worlds various monsters of the night, few ambitions burned as fiercely as that of Vlad Tepes, the Lord of Vampires, better known as Dracula. After centuries of scheming, exile, and bitter defeats at the hands of mortals and heroes alike (Blade, the X-Men, Doctor Strange, and the Avengers), the vampire monarch finally grew tired of ruling from the darkness. He would no longer hide in ruined castles or lurk in the margins of human society. The time had come to carve out a sovereign nation where the Children of the Night would reign openly.

He chose the Carpathian basin.

It happened fast.

It began quietly, the skies over Romania, Moldova, and parts of western Ukraine, regions already steeped in folklore of strigoi and nosferatu, became the first targets. The skies over head turned dark. Dracula did not come with armies of the living. He came with something far more insidious.

Using ancient sorcery recovered from the pages of the Darkhold and alliances with lesser vampire lords. Dracula unleashed a coordinated ritual. At the time of his attack a mystical darkness blanketed the region.

Communications failed. Satellites went blind.

Government officials in Bucharest and Kyiv began receiving hypnotic visitations in their sleep.

By the time anyone knew what was happening, the takeover was nearly complete.

Key military bases were overrun not by force of arms, but by mass turning. Entire regiments of soldiers awoke as fledgling vampires, bound by blood oath to their new emperor.

Mass executions of human resistors was carried out. May were enslaved to be fed on.

Human politicians who resisted were either drained dry or enthralled. Key postions were converted into temporary daywalkers through a serum, vampires gifted with a specialized abilities allowing them limited function in sunlight, useful as administrators and public faces.

Dracula himself appeared on television from the restored Castle Dracula, that had rose from the mist, his regal form clad in blood-red armor and a cap**e that seemed to drink in light. His voice, rich with centuries of command, echoed across the region

"For too long, my people have been hunted and feared. No more. Today marks the birth of Vampyrsk, a nation where the eternal may walk without shame, and the living may serve with purpose. Those who accept the gift of my kind shall know power. Those who resist shall feed us."

______

The new nation-state of Vampyrsk encompassed roughly 180,000 square kilometers, stretching from the Carpathian Mountains to the Black Sea. Its flag was simple but chilling, a black field with a crimson dragon (the old Tepes symbol) coiled around a silver moon.

Governance operated on a strict hierarchy. Lord Tepes held absolute authority.

Next was The Blood Court. Dracula’s inner circle of ancient vampires and turned superhumans.

The Day Council. Enslaved or willingly converted human officials who handled daylight affairs and international diplomacy.

The Night Legions. Elite vampire warriors, including turned mutants and enhanced soldiers.

Society was restructured around the Red Tithe. A system where every human citizen owed a monthly blood donation in exchange for protection and certain privileges. Those who volunteered for full conversion were fast-tracked into the upper castes. Criminals and dissidents became livestock, kept in captivity.

Technology flourished in strange new directions. Vampire scientists (many turned from former Romanian and Ukrainian research institutes) developed heliocrete a building material that blocked UV rays, allowing vampires to walk streets during the day under permanent overcast skies maintained by weather sorcery. Blood banks became the new currency exchange. Synthetic blood alternatives were banned; Dracula believed true strength came only from the living.

The world recoiled in horror. But Lord Tepes held fast. Any intent to interfere with his new nation would be met with severe consequences.

The European Union condemned the "Vampyric Coup" and attempted sanctions, but found their diplomats returning as thralls. NATO mobilized, only to discover entire battalions wiped out in night raids led by Dracula himself.

Russia claimed the Ukrainian portions as "historically theirs" and attempted a conventional invasion. They lost three divisions in a single night. Dracula broadcast footage of Russian generals kneeling before him, now sporting fangs.

The United States debated intervention. Some politicians called for diplomacy. Others whispered that a contained vampire state might be... useful. After all, Dracula had offered to sell advanced medical blood-products derived from his people’s healing factor.

________

Dracula walked the streets of his new capital, Nocturne (formerly Cluj-Napoca), personally greeting subjects. Some knelt in awe. Others in terror. He seemed almost... content. For the first time in centuries, the monster had a kingdom worthy of his name.

Yet even Dracula knew this was only the beginning.

He thought of expansiom, into Hungary, Serbia, perhaps even Austria. The Lord of Vampires stared out from the highest tower of Castle Dracula as storm clouds gathered over the Carpathians, his red eyes gleaming with ancient hunger.

"The world has had its age of man," he murmured. "Now comes the Long Night."

________

Emma and Tessa watched the news in horror as a reporter screamed over the shrieking blades of a helicopter, her eyes bulging through her skull. Before she can finish signing off, a black flash of light dashes into frame, and the transmission ends. "We are so $%&*ed."

"Absolutely and utterly %#&$ed beyond belief," Sage replies. "Should we even be surprised that “reconvening” to discuss terms just became this? Or is it just that predictable by this point that nothing ever seems to go right for us? We definitely have to do something. We should get the staff together and figure out a game plan."

"He’s already created an international incident. We need X-Force, don’t we? They cannot know we had a hand in his downfall."

"Absolutely. I’ll contact Sam and see who’s still around for an operation."

Chapter 2: Stratego

Chapter Text

The X-Mansion stood bathed in moonlight, its spires cutting into the night sky. Inside, most of the mutants were scattered, resting, or out. Some on missions, others attending to other things. Sage sat alone where HE knew she would be, her fingers dancing across holographic displays, her mind processing terabytes of data with effortless precision.

A distant alarm blared. Then another. Red lights flashed across the board.

Outside, chaos erupted. A horde of undead poured from the tree line, dozens of them, hissing and snarling, pale flesh gleaming under the moon. Some wore tattered Victorian finery, others modern street clothes stained with old blood. They smashed through the grounds, shattering windows, tearing up the lawn, and overwhelming the automated sentinels. Alarms wailed as younger X-Men rushed out to meet them, students and junior members forming a desperate defensive line.

“Keep them busy,” a velvet voice whispered on the night wind.

High above, perched on the roof like a gargoyle made flesh, Dracula watched. The Lord of Vampires had traded his usual regal cape for shadows, his crimson eyes glowing faintly. He had studied the X-Men long enough to know their weaknesses. Tonight, he needed only one thing from them.

Sage.

With a swirl of his cloak, he dropped silently through a shattered skylight, landing in the upper corridors without a sound. The screams and sounds of battle outside masked his movements perfectly. A pair of security drones rounded the corner, only to be reduced to sparking wreckage by a casual flick of his clawed hand. Their systems died before they could even register his presence.

He moved like liquid night through the halls, past framed portraits of fallen heroes and empty classrooms. A young mutant, some kind of a speedster, blurred past him on the way to the fight. Dracula reached out and snatched him slaughtering him with ease.

The doors to Sage's control room were sealed, reinforced with the best tech the X-Men could afford. Dracula smiled, revealing fangs like polished daggers. He placed one pale hand on the metal.

“Open.”

Ancient sorcery overcame the modern security. The locks melted under unholy pressure. The doors hissed apart.

Sage spun in her chair, already on her feet, combat protocols flooding her mind. Data streams poured across her retinas.

“Sage” Dracula’s voice rolled like distant thunder, cultured and ancient. “What the White Queen sees in you, I do not know. She is magnificent beauty and grace, she deserves a suitor that meets her on her level.

She didn’t waste words. Sage lunged, striking with precise, augmented martial skill enhanced by her perfect recall of every fighting style she’d ever studied. Her fist connected with his jaw, once, twice. Dracula barely moved. He caught her third strike, his grip like iron wrapped in velvet.

“You fight well,” he murmured, almost admiringly. “But you are still flesh and blood. You are beneath me."

Outside, the vampire horde surged harder, drawing more X-Men away from the mansion. A roar echoed across the grounds, beams of red light flashed, lightning lit up the sky. But they were stretched thin.

Sage activated an emergency beacon with a thought, only for Dracula’s other hand to clamp over her temple. Dark energy crackled. Her mental shields, formidable as they were, buckled under the weight of centuries of vampiric will.

“You will serve a greater purpose in death,” he whispered. “My empire requires the White Queen…and I require her admiration. Your loss will lead her to realize this is how things should be."

With inhuman speed, he swept her into his arms. Sage struggled, but his hypnotic gaze held her consciousness in check just long enough. Black mist swirled around them both as Dracula invoked an ancient translocation spell.

By the time the X-Men fought back the last of the vampire horde and realized the true target, the mansion was silent once more. The control room stood empty, screens still flickering with half processed data.

Dracula was already far away, a shadow vanishing into the night with his prize.

______

Preoccupied by the vampires that await the precise moment she was not in her room, the White Queen fought her way to the control room with open skin hands and closed diamond fists. She had felt Sage's telepathic cry for help, eventually compelling mutant children to use their powers more efficiently than they were. They'd forgive the intrusion, surely. Survival was paramount. She found the melted lock and knocked over chair with splashes of blood where she was cut across the face. She was gone. She tried to scream, but no words emerged as she collapsed to the floor.

"Gone."

Chapter 3: Nocturne in the Moonlight

Chapter Text

She was gone. The one woman who understood her. The one woman who never questioned her, never doubted her allegiance to mutantkind, never entertained the notion that she was a villain. The Black Queen, the Mutant Supercomputer, Teresia Karisik, was gone. Taken by the forces the dwell in the darkness, those who slither in the shadows.

Vampires. Though she was often called one metaphorically, she in truth had never enjoyed their folklore. Now, a grudge had been formed for life.

So what is a White Queen to do when her partner is taken?

She takes her back.

A knock is heard at the door to her home, the knock of a fierce but kind Southern man.

"Come in, Sam. It's urgent."

He opens the door and walks in, slight wear from conflict with the vampires, but at least the goggles on his head are unharmed.

"Ya called, Miss Frost?"

"I did. Sit down."

He takes a seat on her couch, with her standing over him.

"I'll be blunt, Sam, because there is no time to waste. Dracula's attack on the mansion was all a distraction."

She projects images of the destroyed control room into his mind.

"We need X-Force. We are getting her back. Gather a team, as we leave tomorrow morning. I am not asking you right now, I am telling you."

"Sounds like Burke was right, Ah would be puttin t’gether another X-Force. Ah can get a team together before sunrise, dontcha worry ‘bout that Ma’am."

"Good. We leave at ten in the morning on the dot. I will leave without you, Sam. Do not be late."

She looks away and takes a swig of her flask.

"Sorry. I don't mean to be stern or mean, I just... I need her back, Sam. I can't lose her."

"Ah understand. Can’t imagine what Ah’d do if Tabby was taken from me like this… we’ll get her back, Ah promise on mah Mama’s life. Ah’ve already got a strike team in mind, ain’t gonna be hard ta find em round here."

"Good. Now go!"

She practically shoves him out the door, unusually brusque for the White Queen.

"And thank you, Sam. Truly."

"Anytime, Ah like ta help."

He leaves to go find a few select people.
